about: SHARED GOLDEN TABLE for the caller-credential module. development-vessel owns src/lib/caller-credential.ts; goal-host-vessel carries a byte-for-byte copy (src/caller-credential.ts, a header naming the source, then the same bytes). This file is identical in both repos (development-vessel test/fixtures/caller-credential-cases.json, goal-host-vessel test/fixtures/caller-credential-cases.json). Each repo's golden test runs every case against its own module and asserts module_sha256 is the sha256 of the module bytes (goal-host: the bytes after the copy header), so an edit to either side reds that side until this table is re-pinned, and re-pinning in one repo without the other reds the other side's sibling-parity check wherever both checkouts sit side by side. Identity is a stub: it authenticates keys that start with golden-valid-, refuses the rest with HTTP 401, and answers per the case's identity mode.
mutating_primitives_include_about: Every name here must be a member of the module's MUTATING_PRIMITIVES and so be gated as a write (isWritePointerType). dispatch_goal is here because it forwards a goal to goal-host /run-goal with the vessel's own fleet key: ungated, an unauthenticated caller starts a walk as the vessel (qa ruling: wherever MUTATING_PRIMITIVES lives, a golden row asserts dispatch_goal is in it). http_fetch is here because it attaches the vessel's fleet key to loopback targets. feature_compose and gap_to_feature are here because they draft, verify and land code changes through the vessel's in-process cutover: ungated, any caller starts a compose (and the route derives `directed` only from an operator credential).
